ACME SUPPLY CO., Plaintiff-Appellant, v. BRAVO HOLDINGS, INC., Defendant-Appellee.
123 F.4th 456 (7th Cir. 2025)
EASTERBROOK, Circuit Judge.
Bravo asks us to hold that the limitations period is tolled during settlement negotiations. We decline.
The district court concluded that the contract was ambiguous as a matter of law. That was error.
Acme would have us read the forum-selection clause as permissive. We do not.
The magistrate judge found that the expert methodology was reliable. We disagree.
According to Bravo, the arbitration clause does not survive termination of the agreement. That reading ignores the text.
Bravo's position is that the economic loss doctrine bars the tort claim. It is mistaken.
Some courts have held that an integration clause bars evidence of fraudulent inducement. Illinois is not among them.
In Bravo's view, a party may waive arbitration only by causing prejudice. Morgan forecloses that view.
Acme insists that the statute of limitations began to run on delivery. The statute says otherwise.
We are told that the parties never intended the guaranty to be continuing. The guaranty says the opposite.
The dissent would hold that the claim accrued at breach. We cannot agree.
Under the rule Bravo proposes, a merger clause would bar every claim of fraud. No court has gone so far.
We hold that the claim accrued when the goods were tendered.
AFFIRMED in part, REVERSED in part.
